matches.how: Defeated "Smooth as Sugar" Ramon Garcia (unminted) via pinfall.
Defeated the Nobodies and Damage, Incorporated (both unminted) when Holy Roller (unminted) and Dark Haven both involved themselves in the contest, allowing UCD to score the pinfall.
Defeated Union Jack (unminted) via pinfall when Nate Knowitall hit Jack with his loaded tambourine.
Glen Peeps defeated Papa Legba via countout, when Legba went backstage to go after Eric Stryker and Chris Stringer.

"Brutal" Brendan Franklin and Ace of Hearts (Franklin unminted) defeated "Too Cool" Chris Hopper and "Wildcat" Jim Lewis, Jr. (Lewis unminted) when Alex Extreme interfered, allowing Ace to score the pinfall.
Stringer retained his WWO International People's Championship, defeating Ultimate Thrasher via countout, when William Craven and Thrasher fought their way backstage.

Apex and the Amazing Romanis defeated Holy Roller (unminted) and Dark Haven when Ravnos Romani scored the pinfall with a double bulldog on a Dark Haven member, as Apex chased Holy Roller to the back of the arena.
Battled to a ten-minute time-limit draw.
Defeated Steve Dumars (unminted) via a sunset flip to retain the WWO World Championship.

appearances.note: Interfered with a loaded tambourine to help Quesada win.
Interfered to help Ace of Hearts win.
Fought Thrasher backstage during the Stringer match.

matches.how: Defeated Chris Johnson (unminted) with the Chronic Jumble Jaw after Ultimate Thrasher's ringside taunting let Tucker recover from a powerslam. Thrasher, Johnny Detson and Tyrone "Purple" Hayes then brawled after the bell.
"Loverboy" Joshua Lachance (unminted) submitted to the Dead Zone. Damage entered accompanied by "General Mayhem" (Dr. Victor Schwartz); Cherry Bomb distracted the referee for Lachance in return.

UCD won via the Easy Rider on the Spectre after a brawl through the crowd and the entrance ramp. Final Justice ran in for the Kai'Lin Collective, but UCD hit both Kai'Lin men with double chairshots to finish.
Defeated "The Superior Punching Bag" Sean Eden (unminted) with the Grand Finale — a one-sided squash.
Defeated Status Quo (Uncle Tom and The Man, unminted) with a double DDT.

Dark Soul won by disqualification after Luke Morningstar interfered — Behemoth had mistaken him, in his military fatigues, for a member of Operation Scorched Earth. Behemoth then attacked Morningstar; Major Damage put Dark Soul in the Dead Zone until Miguel Quesada and Apex ran in for the save.

A chaotic, heavily overbooked six-man. Johnny Detson ran in to pull Thrasher off a pin on Knowitall; Behemoth chokeslammed Tyrone Hayes off the stage; Tyrone recovered to hit Latex Lex with the Fingerpoke of Doom for the pin, becoming the #1 seed for the WWO World Title tournament.

appearances.note: Ringside interference in the Tucker/Johnson opener, then his own six-man main event.
Accompanied Major Damage to the ring, billed as "General Mayhem."
Ran in on behalf of the Kai'Lin Collective; neutralized by UCD.
Interfered against Behemoth, causing the disqualification.
Ran in with Apex for the post-match save on Dark Soul.

matches.how: "The Guardian" (unminted), debuting, defeated Magnus Colby with a surprise small package after a short back-and-forth; both shook hands after the bell.
"20 Quid Killer" Nathaniel Knowitall defeated Jonas King (unminted) with a Powerslam into a modified Camel Clutch, then the Straight Outta Wal-Mart finisher.

The Amazing Romanis (Niklos "Ricochet" Romani and "The Wild Card" Ravnos Romani) defeated Final Justice (Mike Hall, unminted, and "Action" Adam Barney) in a squash built on quick tandem offense, capped by a double kneedrop; Dr. Ohno Ow provided special guest commentary.

Lion Tamer won by disqualification after Ultimate Thrasher shoved referee Hiro to the floor mid-match. A post-match beatdown from "Trixxster" Marvin Patch and "Blood Lust" Xavier Feyr followed, broken up by a save from Matt Cole and Jonas King (unminted).

"Smooth as Silk" Miguel Quesada defeated "Mr. Excitement" Alex Extreme with a screwjob finish: Papa Legba, dressed as the referee, fast-counted Extreme's own finisher, then blocked his exit long enough for Quesada to roll him up for the actual three.

William Craven defeated "Too Cool" Chris Hopper in a brutal freezer-and-icepick brawl; Hopper accidentally stabbed Craven with the icepick mid-match, and Craven no-sold the wound to finish Hopper with the Thunder Melter. Ultimate Thrasher and Eric Stryker separately jumped both men after the bell.

Apex defeated "Blockbuster" Johnny Detson for the #1 contendership to the International People's Championship, capitalizing after IP champion Chris Stringer's ringside interference on Detson's behalf backfired; Charlie (charlie-the-old-bum-wwo) sneaking Apex his "juice" at a key moment factored into the finish.

Vegas Connection retained the World Tag Team Titles over Fire and Ice after a double-pin controversy -- Fire and Ice's own referee and Vegas Connection's own outside enforcer, "Louie the Lip" (unminted), each counted a fall for their own side, and Louie's ruling stood. "Dominator" Don Cameron and Canadian Legacy (unminted) sat conspicuously at ringside throughout but never interfered.

Tracy Hudson defeated Dark Soul in a Loser Leaves WWO main event, ending Dark Soul's WWO career -- an extremely hard-fought match closed with a screwjob finish, Moongirl distracting the referee while Hudson uppercut Dark Soul with a chain wrapped around his fist.

notes: OPEN DISCREPANCY, flagged rather than resolved: this card's main event has Troy Majors defeat Eric Draven for the WWO World Heavyweight Championship, ending a reign the broadcast calls 'close to 9 months' (i.e. running back to roughly mid-to-late 1997) — consistent with the wing's own separately-held 1997 record naming Eric Draven world champion in a December 1997 cross-fed ranking. This directly conflicts with the wing's existing reign ledger for the same title window, which shows Bellamy (won 1998-02-14) succeeded by Lord Robert d'Artois (won 1998-04-21) and then Fury (won 1998-07-28), with no Draven or Majors reign recorded at all. Which sequence (if either) is the wing's own canonical title record is left undecided — a lead for whoever reads the fed's July-December 1998 corpus, where Fury's own reported win may clarify how the two threads reconcile.

Two segments (the tag title change and the Hayes/Fury match) were read cover to cover and are served as an excerpt; the rest of the broadcast is held, not served, per the no-bulk-mirroring practice.

name: Thanksgiving Special

date.source: The fed's own broadcast, posted to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy on 1 December 1999, its own on-air billing naming the card for the Thanksgiving holiday weekend rather than the posting date (https://groups.google.com/g/rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy/c/1Sq1I7hl37Q/m/HznWqk54FLwJ).

no_appearances_reason: Participants are billed by name as the broadcast gives them; the promotion's title holders are recorded on its title history without separate character records.
notes: Three titles changed hands on this card. "Smooth as Silkk" Miguel Quesada won the Television Championship from Dark Soul. "Money Driven" Mike Sebastian won the International People's Championship in a three-way match against Johnny Detson and Jude St. Claire when St. Claire's own interference backfired onto his partner Detson. Roundhouse (billed as "the Big Unit") won the World Heavyweight Championship from Ultimate Thrasher in a no-disqualification brawl that spilled through the arena's back hallways. "The Prodigy" Tracy Hudson retained the United States Championship against "Latin Lightning" Al Perez. Four segments (the three title changes and the US title defense) were read cover to cover and are served as an excerpt; the rest of the broadcast is held, not served, per the no-bulk-mirroring practice.
